display.title: Tanya Shiur 28: Rising Like a Lion, the Beinoni of Chapter 12, and Elul
display.summary_short: A Yiddish shiur: the Rebbe's call to learn more as nights lengthen, Shulchan Aruch HaRav on rising bold as a leopard and strong as a lion, the beinoni in Tanya 12, and Elul.
display.summary_long: Shiur 28 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series, recorded at the end of Av. It opens with the Rebbe's talk of Chamishah Asar B'Av: as the nights grow longer, add to Torah study, both Chassidus and practical halachah, which is why a new class in the Alter Rebbe's Shulchan Aruch was added. On sleep, the speaker explains that as a Jew goes to sleep so he wakes, that the soul ascends at night, and that the right amount of sleep prepares a day of service. The first seif of Hilchos Hashkamas HaBoker follows: be bold as a leopard and do not be shamed by scoffers, be strong as a lion to overcome the yetzer hara every morning, and wake the dawn rather than letting it wake you. The Tanya part continues chapter 12: during davening the beinoni's G-dly soul rules, and afterwards the yetzer hara stirs again. Each small victory brings great joy above, and the beinoni pushes away a stray thought 'with both hands' and is glad to do so. A talk for the coming month of Elul ends the class: the King in the field, the shofar's call to take stock, and wishes for a good inscription.
display.lesson: Each morning and each moment is a new battle with the yetzer hara; win it with boldness and joy, and use the longer nights and the month of Elul to add in Torah and return to Hashem.

date.note: Filename says '29 av 5736'; on air the speaker refers to the coming Rosh Chodesh Elul and a farbrengen that evening.

sources_cited.note: Longer nights: add to Torah study, in Chassidus and in halachah.
